output_full:
coldhubs.com — The Solution – ColdHubs — https://coldhubs.com/our-solution/
(opened by the member, not cited)
Smallholder Cooperative Operations Specialist said about it: The precedent in The Solution – ColdHubs (E43) places clean plastic crates on shelves under a pay-as-you-store daily flat fee per crate, so I use 50 crates at 20.0 kg each for 1000 kg total, staged as 250 kg per day with First-In-First-Out (FIFO, oldest crates sold first) paper tags in the revised steady load with 120mm PU and staged loading pull-down (E28), about 50 shopping bags of maize meal in everyday scale.
Smallholder Cooperative Operations Specialist said about it: The rule in Small-Scale Postharvest Handling Practices (E44) keeps temperate crops near 0 degC but chilling-sensitive crops at 10 degC to 12 degC to avoid injury, so the single 5.0 degC mixed holding is an agreed compromise to hold tomatoes with leafy vegetables, paid by the flat fee in The Solution – ColdHubs (E43) covering reusable crates, twice-daily wall thermometer checks and hose cleaning with early-morning shaded intake.

statements.text: The precedent in The Solution – ColdHubs (E43) places clean plastic crates on shelves under a pay-as-you-store daily flat fee per crate, so I use 50 crates at 20.0 kg each for 1000 kg total, staged as 250 kg per day with First-In-First-Out (FIFO, oldest crates sold first) paper tags in the revised steady load with 120mm PU and staged loading pull-down (E28), about 50 shopping bags of maize meal in everyday scale.

The rule in Small-Scale Postharvest Handling Practices (E44) keeps temperate crops near 0 degC but chilling-sensitive crops at 10 degC to 12 degC to avoid injury, so the single 5.0 degC mixed holding is an agreed compromise to hold tomatoes with leafy vegetables, paid by the flat fee in The Solution – ColdHubs (E43) covering reusable crates, twice-daily wall thermometer checks and hose cleaning with early-morning shaded intake.
